claude.result:
I fixed it: `frai gate init --ci` now creates `.github/workflows/rai-gate.yml`.

**Cause:** the top-level `frai` command also has a `--ci` option. By default, Commander (the argument-parsing library) lets top-level options match anywhere on the command line. So the top-level command took `--ci` and it was never passed to `frai-gate`, which just saw `init`.

**Fix** (`packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts`, 2 lines):
- Added `.enablePositionalOptions()` to the top-level program, so its options only count when they come before a subcommand.
- Added `.passThroughOptions()` to the `gate` command, so everything after `gate` goes to `frai-gate` unchanged.

The same fix covers the other top-level flags too (`--scan`, `--key`, `--global`, etc.), which had the same problem after `gate`. `packages/frai-gate` is untouched.

**Checked:**
- Before the fix, only `FRAI-SPEC.md` was created.
- `pnpm --filter frai build` succeeded.
- After the fix, the same command printed both "Created FRAI-SPEC.md" and "Created .github/workflows/rai-gate.yml", and both files were on disk.
- `frai scan --json` still works, so options on other subcommands are parsed as before.

**Side effect:** a top-level-only flag placed after a subcommand (e.g. `frai docs list --ci`) is no longer silently accepted. Commander will report it as an unknown option. No subcommand used those values anyway.

**Two things to clean up:**
- My first test ran in the repo root by mistake and created a stray `FRAI-SPEC.md`. I deleted it.
- The scratch test folder `.repro-before/` is still in the repo, untracked. The shell's working directory is inside it, so deleting it was blocked. Please remove it with `rm -r .repro-before` from the repo root.

Changed files are `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` and the rebuilt `packages/frai-cli/dist/index.js`. Nothing is committed.
